posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
I actually think that your "very simple tileset" might be shooting you in the foot a bit, here. I've been using XP for years and I'd hesitate to use a tileset like that for fear of getting confused on which tile is which XD As Slim said, you have several all-black tiles, some of which are set to O--make sure that the one in use on your map is the same as the one that you've set the passability of.
Passability is more than just X and O--there are also settings that allow you to walk behind things (priority) and only from certain direction (directional passability). Additionally, layers can complicate passability; for example, if you have a flower tile (O) placed so it overlaps the bottom of a bridge tile (X), you may be able to walk on that bridge tile.
I would export a handful of the Interior tilesets (say maybe Post Town, Port Town, and Snow Town) and create a new tileset using the walls from one, the floor from another, and the shelves and tables from the third. Import that tileset, and try settng the passabiliies based on how they are in the sample tilesets.
Finally--and somewhat unrelated, but important to know--it looks like your tileset includes options for all of he different types of wall edge you might need? There's a much easier way to do that, called an Autotile--all those spaces you've set to X across the top are for Autotiles. I haven't finished my Custom Assets or Database tutorials yet (the ones that would cover making and importing your own tilesets) but
I do have one for mapping
, if you'ld like to see how autotiles are used! They'll save you a lot of time.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body: You probably used that tile as an eraser at some point. XP has an eraser tile built in, it's the top left square of every tileset, next to the autotiles. Make sure that you only use that one as your eraser, and things will be much easier for you!
